Stocks Rose 18 Times Out of 18 After Midterms. Will 2026 Break the Streak?

2026-11-02

Subscribe for one money story a week

About this video

Since 1950, the S&P 500 has been higher one year after every single midterm election: 18 out of 18. The average gain was about 18%, roughly three times a normal year. But the midterm year itself is often bad: in 2022, stocks were down 18.5% by October, then climbed about 21% after the vote. So will 2026 make it 19 for 19? We look at the data, the three main explanations, the fine print, and why 2026 is different. 0:00 Intro: 18 out of 18 0:26 What is a midterm? 0:49 18 green bars 1:30 Normal years vs midterm years 1:47 The twist: the midterm slump 2:18 Why it happens 2:58 The fine print 3:23 Why 2026 is different 3:53 What it means for you 4:21 Recap Data: S&P 500 monthly prices from Robert Shiller's dataset (Yale University, ie_data), price only, monthly averages, through September 2023. Window: October of each midterm year to October one year later, 1950-2018 (18 midterms). 2022 is measured to September 2023, where the dataset ends.
